other_requirements: Must be enrolled (or starting) in a construction-related program or apprenticeship.
name: NAWIC Founders' Scholarship Foundation Scholarships
summary: Scholarships for students and apprentices training for construction careers, including the building trades. The foundation gives more than $600,000 a year.
how_to_apply: Apply online at nfsf.nawic.org between September and early March for the next school year.

other_requirements: Must be enrolled in a plumbing or HVAC program, or be an apprentice with a PHCC member contractor.
name: PHCC Educational Foundation Scholarships
summary: About 75 awards a year for students in plumbing or HVAC programs at trade schools and community colleges, and for apprentices working for PHCC member contractors.
how_to_apply: Apply online: answer five short questions about your interest in the trade and send one letter of recommendation from an instructor, advisor or employer.

name: GE Aerospace-Reagan Workforce Readiness Scholarship
sponsor: Ronald Reagan Presidential Foundation and GE Aerospace
summary: For high school seniors heading into technical training or certifications for aircraft maintenance, avionics, welding, CNC machining, electrical, industrial maintenance, robotics, quality inspection or logistics careers.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the foundation's page (run by Kaleidoscope). Sign up there to be told when the next application opens.
amount_text: Up to $10,000 a year, for up to two years

other_requirements: High school diploma or GED by the time you start, an approved FAFSA, and a vehicle technician program at an accredited school. U.S. citizens, permanent residents and DACA students.
name: TechForce Foundation Scholarships
summary: Need-based scholarships and grants for students training to be automotive, diesel, collision, aviation, marine or motorcycle technicians.
how_to_apply: Create a free TechForce account, build a profile and apply under Scholarships. Applications run in cycles all year; check the decision-day calendar.
amount_text: Varies (about $3 million awarded so far in 2026)

other_requirements: High school graduate, GED or graduating senior; drug free with a safe driving record; at an accredited technical college within 50 miles of Sawnee EMC in Cumming.
name: Sawnee EMC Brian Johnson Memorial Lineworker Scholarship
summary: Helps students in an electrical lineworker program at a technical college near Cumming, Georgia, such as Lanier Technical College or North Georgia Technical College. Paid to the college for tuition, books and fees.
how_to_apply: Download the application from Sawnee EMC's page and mail it to the Sawnee Electric Membership Foundation.
deadline_text: Ask Sawnee EMC for this year's date
